 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, OT Keagan Trost, and DE Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 8 against the Chargers. 
 Parkinson will miss at least one game with a rib injury he sustained last week against the Raiders. His absence could have a big impact on playing time for both Davis Allen — who had two touchdown grabs last week — and Tyler Higbee, the de facto TE1 in the LA offense. Both tight ends are better options against the Chargers with Parkinson sidelined. 
 -  Denny Carter 
 Source:  Nate Atkins

 Related Player News
 Tyler Higbee 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Tyler Higbee caught 1-of-2 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 8 win against the Chargers. 
 It was another disappointing outing for Higbee. This one came with Colby Parkinson (ribs) sidelined. Davis Allen had two catches on two targets for eight yards. Higbee now hasn’t had more than 25 yards receiving in a game since the beginning of October, and has lost opportunities with the Rams going run heavy in recent weeks. Higbee won’t be a fantasy option in Week 9 against the Commanders. 
 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Week 8 against the Chargers. 
 Parkinson gutted out an injury to his midsection against the Raiders a week ago when he was in and out of the lineup while clearly dealing with significant discomfort. He was unable to practice through Thursday this week, prompting the questionable designation ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Chargers. Already down multiple primary pass catchers, the Rams could see further concentration of volume should Parkinson miss, a situation that could also pave the way for Davis Allen to see an uptick in opportunities in the 12- and 13-personnel-heavy Rams offense. Fantasy managers likely won’t get further updates on Parkinson’s status before the team releases inactives 90-minutes prior to first kick. 
 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Thursday. 
 Parkinson will have one more chance to get back no the practice field Friday to avoid an injury designation entering the weekend. The veteran tight end was in and out of the team’s Week 7 game with the injury but managed to finish it, apparently feeling much worse after the adrenaline wore off. Fantasy managers of Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will want to track Parkinson’s status closely to end the week. An absence from Parkinson could also bring Davis Allen into the fantasy spotlight after the young tight end scored twice against the Raiders. 
 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Colby Parkinson (ribs) will not practice on Wednesday. 
 Parkinson has meaningfully contributed to the Rams’ offense in each of the last two weeks, but he is now at risk of missing his team’s Week 8 game against the Chargers. Were Parkinson to sit out on Sunday, Tyler Higbee would likely benefit. 
 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders. 
 Parkinson was in and out of the game with various injuries, picking up a new ailment on seemingly every reception. Parkinson logged 16 pass routes while Tyler Higbee led the team’s tight ends with 18 routes. Davis Allen, meanwhile, ran a route on 12 of the Rams’ drop backs and caught two touchdowns from Matthew Stafford. Parkinson should be a viable desperation option in deeper formats next week against the Chargers if the Rams keep using three tight end sets at a high rate. He has ten receptions over his past two outings. 
 Davis Allen 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #87 
 Davis Allen caught 4-of-5 targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders. 
 The Rams in Week 7 resorted to a heavy dose of three tight end sets with Davante Adams sidelined with a long-term hamstring injury. That led to 12 pass routes for Allen, fewer than both Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee. He caught two red zone touchdowns from Matthew Stafford, however, seeing a look on 33 percent of his routes. Allen will be tough to trust as a fantasy option unless or until his snaps and routes increase. He could be a deep league option in Week 8 against the Chargers, however. 
 Tyler Higbee 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Tyler Higbee caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 7 win against the Raiders. 
 It was Davis Allen who caught two of Matthew Stafford’s three touchdown tosses as the Rams leaned into heavy three tight end-set usage with Davante Adams sidelined indefinitely with a hamstring injury. Though Higbee led Rams tight ends in pass routes, his lack of red zone involvement left him out in the statistical cold. Trying to figure out which LA tight end is going to go off in a given week is going to be a continual headache for fantasy gamers in the coming weeks. 
 Tyler Higbee 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #89 
 Tyler Higbee caught 4-of-4 targets for 22 yards and one lost fumble in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. 
 Higbee lost volume to Colby Parkinson in this one. Higbee also had the ball ripped from his possession by Cardinals LB Cody Simon while trying to fall forward for extra yards on the Rams’ seventh drive, further reducing his fantasy output. With Parkinson playing well, Higbee is a shakier, low-end TE1 against the Raiders next week. 
 Colby Parkinson 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #84 
 Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. 
 Parkinson played effectively against the Cardinals’ zone coverage this afternoon. He bagged a first down after finding a soft spot downfield on the Rams’ fourth drive, and deftly hurdled a defender on a one-yard gain a few plays later. His touchdown occurred on the Rams’ final possession and required post-catch effort, barreling through contact and extending for the score. Parkinson is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Raiders in Week 7. 
 Davis Allen 
 LA 
 Tight End 
 #87 
 Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report. 
 He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

 Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
 The veteran receiver played through both ailments in Week 8 but was limited to only 54 percent of the team’s offensive snaps in a blowout win. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status in the coming days, with the expectation that he continues to play through the injuries against the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

 Chris Rodriguez (hand) was limited on Monday’s estimated practice report.
 This appears to be a non-issue as the veteran change of pace back should be fine for Thursday Night Football against the Ravens. Of greater concern was the absence of lead back Bayshul Tuten, something fantasy managers of both players will want to monitor as Thursday draw nearer. Rodriguez would seemingly be in line for a featured role if Tuten is unable to play on a short week.
 -  Mark Garcia

 Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a “DNP” on Monday’s estimated practice report.
 Tuten briefly left the team’s Week 8 win in the first quarter but returned to amass 159 total yards and two touchdowns against the overmatched Colts. Fantasy managers will want to track his status closely as the team makes a quick turn to face the Ravens on Thursday Night Football.

 The fact he was listed as limited and not a “DNP” likely signals a more modest injury and we would expect Hill to suit up when the Ravens take on the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. Either way, fantasy managers likely have better options at the position.

 Mark Andrews (hand) was listed as a full participant on Monday’s estimated injury report.
 That keeps the veteran tight end on track to suit up in Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football. Andrews has struggled to return usable fantasy weeks throughout his age-31 season, with the team now down to their third, potentially fourth, quarterback for Thursday’s game. he can safely be left on fantasy benches on the short week.
 -  Mark Garcia

 Zach Charbonnet 
 SEA 
 Running Back 
 #26 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Zach Charbonnet (knee) and Jadarian Price (chest) are active for Week 8 against the Bears.
 Charbonnet makes his season debut after a suffering a torn ACL late in the 2025 season while Price returns from short-term injure reserve due to a chest injury. Emmanuel Wilson and George Holani had held down the backfield in the absence of the two top backs, leaving an uncertain situation regarding expected backfield utilization when the Seahawks take on the Bears in a marquee matchup. Inactive for the Seahawks are QB Drew Lock, LB Uchenna Nwosu, WR Rashid Shaheed, RB Velus Jones Jr., OT Charles Cross, G Beau Stephens, and NT Brandon Pili.
 -  Mark Garcia 
 More Zach Charbonnet News
 Kyle Monangai 
 CHI 
 Running Back 
 #25 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, QB Case Keenum, DB Malik Muhammad, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and OL Jordan van den Berg inactive for Week 8 against the Seahawks.
 No real surprises here after Monangai was ruled out for Week 8 on Saturday, leaving D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson to handle backfield duties in a difficult matchup against the Seahawks. The two had operated in a loosely split backfield before Week 7, during which Swift saw workhorse usage in a tight game against the Patriots. It would appear likely that Swift will once again see the bulk of the work considering the opponent, making him a surefire RB2 with RB1 upside to cap the Week 8 festivities. 
 -  Mark Garcia 
 More Kyle Monangai News
 Tyler Loop 
 BAL 
 Kicker 
 #33 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Jesse Minter said the team is considering injured reserve for Tyler Loop (undisclosed).
 Loop suffered an undisclosed injury in the Week 8 loss to the Bills, something that is reportedly serious enough to warrant injured reserve consideration. When asked if Jake Moody would be kicking on Thursday Night Football against the Jaguars, Minter replied with a simple, “At this point, yes.” The Ravens were dealt numerous injury issues in their loss to the Bills as they lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley, with third string rookie Joe Fagnano also emerging dinged up after taking numerous hard sacks.
 -  Mark Garcia 
 More Tyler Loop News
 Joe Fagnano 
 BAL 
 Quarterback 
 #12 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Jesse Minter said Joe Fagnano (ankle) is “dealing with some things physically” but has a chance to start in Week 9.
 Whelp, that isn’t exactly a ringing endorsement for the rookie quarterback’s chances of starting under center for the Ravens when they host the Jaguars on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 9. The team lost both Lamar Jackson to a season-ending thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley to a turf toe injury in their Week 8 loss to the Bills, now in desperate need of a viable quarterback option as they fight for their playoff lives. It is possible the team addresses the position through trade with just over a week until the trade deadline, although that is unlikely to help them on a short week. More to come in what quickly became a dire situation in Baltimore. Fagnano was officially listed as limited on the team’s estimated practice report Monday.
 -  Mark Garcia 
 Injury 
 More Joe Fagnano News
 David Njoku 
 LAC 
 Tight End 
 #83 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 Jim Harbaugh said the team will open the 21-day practice window for David Njoku this week.
 Njoku has been on the shelf since being placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 3, with the potential to return following five missed games plus the team’s Week 7 bye. The team will have 21 days to activate him from short-term injured reserve, meaning Njoku is not guaranteed to be activated in time for Week 9 against the Texans. Fantasy managers that have held Njoku through his time on injured reserve can continue patiently waiting for his return while those in shallower leagues can consider adding him from waivers before he is activated.
 -  Mark Garcia 
 Source:  Noah Furtado
